traceability.evidence:
1) Story file present: - docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md exists and defines the required behavior, formats, and examples for @story and @req annotations.
2) Core rule implementation: - File: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Top-level JSDoc explicitly tags this story and requirements: """ * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Define clear format rules for @story and @req annotations * @req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION - Validate annotation syntax matches specification * @req REQ-PATH-FORMAT - Validate @story paths follow expected patterns * @req REQ-REQ-FORMAT - Validate @req identifiers follow expected patterns * @req REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT - Handle annotations split across multiple lines * @req REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING - Support reasonable variations in whitespace and formatting * @req REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY - Provide specific error messages for different format violations """ - Key functionality: - normalizeCommentLine(rawLine: string): handles empty lines, strips leading '*', and preserves @story/@req tokens → flexible parsing of various comment styles (REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING). - collapseAnnotationValue(value: string): collapses all internal whitespace (value.replace(/\s+/g, "")) so multi-line values become a single logical token → REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT. - validateStoryAnnotation(context, comment, rawValue): - Trims rawValue; if empty, reports messageId "invalidStoryFormat" with data.details from buildStoryErrorMessage("missing", null): "Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like \"docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md\"." → matches the story’s invalid examples and REQ-PATH-FORMAT. - Collapses whitespace and enforces pattern: /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/ → ensures relative path under docs/stories, release number, -DEV-, slug, and .story.md extension → REQ-PATH-FORMAT. - Rejects paths containing whitespace after initial trim, and uses getFixedStoryPath for safe suffix normalization (.story → .story.md, .md → .story.md, no extension → .story.md) while skipping any value containing ".." (path traversal). - validateReqAnnotation(context, comment, rawValue): - Trims rawValue; if empty, reports invalidReqFormat with message built by buildReqErrorMessage("missing", null): "Missing requirement ID for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like \"REQ-EXAMPLE\"." → REQ-REQ-FORMAT. - Enforces /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ for collapsed value → checks REQ-* pattern (uppercase letters, numbers, dashes only). - processComment(context, comment): - Splits comment.value into lines, normalizes each, detects @story/@req, and collects continuation lines into a PendingAnnotation. - Calls validateStoryAnnotation / validateReqAnnotation when an annotation is complete. - Handles empty/malformed lines without throwing → satisfies Error Handling acceptance criterion (graceful handling of malformed comments) and REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT / REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING. - meta.messages: - invalidStoryFormat: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." - invalidReqFormat: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." → combined with detailed "details" strings from helper functions provides clear, specific, and consistent error messages for different violations (missing vs invalid, story vs req) → REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY and User Experience acceptance criterion. - Rule create(context) walks Program() and inspects all comments via sourceCode.getAllComments(), so it validates annotations regardless of whether they attach to functions or branches.
3) Integration with other rules and plugin config: - File: src/index.ts - RULE_NAMES includes "valid-annotation-format": const RULE_NAMES = [ "require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference", ]; - Dynamic loader: rules[name] = require(`./rules/${name}`).default ?? mod; → ensures valid-annotation-format is part of the exported plugin rules. - TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES maps "traceability/valid-annotation-format" to "warn"; recommended and strict configs include this map, so the format rule runs alongside function and branch rules. - Additional rules present and integrated: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts (function @story enforcement) - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts (function @req enforcement) - src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts (branch-level @story/@req enforcement) → valid-annotation-format provides the syntax layer that works with annotations detected/enforced by these rules, matching the Integration acceptance criterion.
4) Tests explicitly tied to this story: - File: tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - Header: """ * Tests for: docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Verify valid-annotation-format rule enforces annotation format syntax """ - Uses ESLint RuleTester with rule from ../../src/rules/valid-annotation-format. - Valid cases: - `// @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` → confirms accepted story path format. - `// @req REQ-EXAMPLE` → confirms accepted REQ-* identifier format. - Block comments with both annotations and single-line values. - Multi-line story path split across lines: `@story docs/stories/005.0-` / `DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md` → validates multi-line story handling. - Multi-line req ID split across lines: `@req REQ-` / `EXAMPLE` → validates multi-line @req handling. - JSDoc-style comment with leading '*' and extra spaces → validates flexible parsing of whitespace and comment style. - Invalid cases match story’s invalid examples: - Missing story path: `// @story` and block `@story` → expect invalidStoryFormat with the "Missing story path..." detail. - Invalid story suffix `.story` and missing extension → expect invalidStoryFormat and precise auto-fix output adding `.story.md`. - Path traversal: `// @story ../docs/stories/...` → expect invalidStoryFormat with invalid-path detail, no auto-fix. - Missing req ID: `// @req` and `// @req ` and block `@req` → expect invalidReqFormat with "Missing requirement ID..." detail. - Invalid req ID format: `// @req invalid-format` and multi-line `invalid-` / `format` → expect invalidReqFormat with detailed explanation of expected REQ-EXAMPLE pattern (uppercase letters, numbers, dashes). - These tests demonstrate coverage of all key requirements: REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY.

traceability.notes: The story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION has been fully implemented. The dedicated ESLint rule valid-annotation-format strictly validates @story and @req annotations against the specified patterns, supports multi-line values and flexible comment styles, and produces clear, specific error messages for missing and invalid formats. It is integrated into the plugin alongside the function and branch annotation rules, and a targeted RuleTester test suite explicitly tied to this story comprehensively covers valid/invalid cases and error messages. Jest tests run successfully with no reported failures, providing concrete evidence that the implementation meets all the story’s functional, quality, integration, user experience, error handling, and documentation-related acceptance criteria.
